column1: # Open gaps (tools/bench.sh): a shortfall that is known and not yet closed. One line per gap, tabs between:
# linux: the metric misses its target against Linux's locked number (bench/reference.tsv); the bound is the
# ratio to that number it may not exceed. ratchet: it is worse than its own best (bench/ratchet.tsv); the bound
# is the value it may not pass, on the host named ("-": any host, a count). While a metric is no worse than its
# bound a run reports it OPEN and passes; past it, ERROR. A line is added by a commit that says why, tightened
# or removed by `bench.sh --update-ratchet`, and never loosened. No milestone is declared over a line of a
# metric it requires. Each line is work owed: close it in Silica, or decide the cost and move its ratchet with
# The bounds below are from the sessions of 2026-11-22 (the single-processor and device values from a session
# that had a stray process on one measured core, which those paths do not use: tighten them from the first

column5: 9.15 us against Linux 10.23 (target 8.70). 2026-11-23: the receive queue's interrupt is watched (IrqWatch, IrqQuiet: ARCHITECTURE.md section 7), so a processor idling for a frame sees the device write it instead of waiting for the interrupt; bench.sh --compare HEAD in one run: 9.32 to 9.14 us (-1.9%), confined 9.38 to 9.17, where the same change took 1.2 us off a block read. The round trip has more on it than the completion: the client's transmit, the echo on the host, the network queue's two programs. Waits for: the round trip taken apart by stage as blkcheck's read is (netcheck's traced frames), then the stage that is Silica's made shorter

boot went from 13.8 to 20.5 ms since the ratchet was set at the M2 exit; the cause is not attributed and no commit weighed the cost. Waits for: the cause found among the kernel and init commits since the M2 exit that touch boot, then won back or its cost written beside the ratchet 2026-11-23, attributed by the loader's and kernel's new boot lines (bench.sh --now --fresh --only boot, five boots): the firmware's ExitBootServices 12.5 to 14.2 ms of the loader's 14.2 to 14.5 (OVMF parking seven processors; 1.7 ms on one); the IOMMU's set-up 3.3 ms, or 6.1 to 7.3 ms in two boots of five (QEMU's VT-d model switching every device's address space on the root table, the context invalidation and translation on: the specification's minimum sequence); everything else in loader and kernel about 1 ms. The I/O APIC's 2.8 ms stall is gone (pins already masked are no longer written). Measured 19.58 ms now, past this bound (the gate is red): the bound is one fortunate run's. The record of 13.77 ms predates the IOMMU (firmware exit 12.5 + kernel 1.2). Waits for: the owner's decision whether this metric counts firmware and emulator time, and the IOMMU's commands made cheaper for the emulator without dropping any the specification requires 2026-11-24, an idle host (other programs 0.41 processors busy, the desktop locked): 22.34 ms, worse than this bound and than the 19.58 already recorded; the loader and the boot path of the kernel unchanged since (kernel commits of 11-24: CapNotice, the page-fault benchmark, test-only changes). Still waits for the same: the decision on firmware and emulator time, and the IOMMU set-up made cheaper for the emulator

2026-11-23: 949,100 a second against its best 1,036,366. Not this session's kernel changes: bench.sh --compare b6d1fd4,1ccc2f2 in one run (an idle host) measured 981,100 before them and 960,600 after, -2.1%, within the noise; the kernel from before them is itself 5% under the ratchet today, so the host moved (the full run's warning of 7.3 processors busy with other programs was bench.sh counting its own guests, fixed since). Waits for: the ratchet's run repeated on an idle host with the kernel it was set on, to say whether the host or the kernel moved, then won back or its cost written beside the ratchet

2026-11-24, first measurement (bench.sh --now --linux --runs 3 --only http,tcp,boot_server): the guest's processors per GiB read at 200 MB/s, 3,228 ms (3,152 to 3,792) against Linux's 805.9, 4.0 times. Before the session: 4.50 s at 2 processors untimed, then 3.09 with the transmit offloads. A profile at 200 MB/s (perf, guest samples): 71% of the guest's cycles in the idle watch (Hal::idle), which grows to its 200 us cap when completions come every few microseconds, on every processor that sees them; VM exits mostly PAUSE. A cap of 20 us cut the cost by a third untimed and left every latency metric unchanged in the sweep (bench.sh --sweep IDLE_WATCH_MAX=20000,200000), but depth-32 block reads lost 5.6% (confined 2.7%): not taken. Waits for: the watch spending only what the halt it avoids costs (a cap from the measured halt and wake, or fewer processors watching one device), measured by this metric and the sweep's, then netd's copies
